title.zh: 卷83下 外戚下:高肇 于勁 胡國珍 李延實
title.en: Volume 83b: Families of Imperial Consorts 2 - Gao Zhao, Yu Jin, Hu Guozhen, Li Yanshi
title.raw: 卷83下 外戚下:高肇 于勁 胡國珍 李延實 Volume 83b: Families of Imperial Consorts 2 - Gao Zhao, Yu Jin, Hu Guozhen, Li Yanshi

sentences.zh: 高肇 于勁 胡國珍 李延寔

translations.literal: Gao Zhao, Yu Jin, Hu Guozhen, Li Yanshi
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao, Yu Jin, Hu Guozhen, and Li Yanshi

sentences.zh: 高肇，字首文，文昭皇太后之兄也。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao, courtesy name Shouwen, was the elder brother of Empress Dowager Wenzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao, whose courtesy name was Shouwen, was the elder brother of Empress Dowager Wenzhao.

sentences.zh: 自云本勃海蓨人，五世祖顧，晉永嘉中避亂入高麗。

translations.literal: He claimed to be originally from Tiao in Bohai; his fifth-generation ancestor Gu, during the Yongjia era of Jin, fled turmoil and entered Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from Tiao in Bohai; during the Jin dynasty's Yongjia era his fifth-generation ancestor Gu had fled the turmoil and taken refuge in Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 父颺，字法脩。

translations.literal: His father Yang, courtesy name Faxian.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Yang, whose courtesy name was Faxian.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，與弟乘信及其鄉人韓內、冀富等入國，拜厲威將軍、河間子，乘信明威將軍，俱待以客禮，賜奴婢牛馬綵帛。

translations.literal: In the early years of Emperor Gaozu, together with his younger brother Chengxin and fellow townsmen Han Nei, Ji Fu, and others, he entered the state; he was appointed Bulwark-General and Marquis of Hejian, Chengxin was appointed Illustrious Might General, and all were received with guest ceremony and granted slaves, cattle, horses, and colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Gaozu's reign he came to the Wei state with his younger brother Chengxin and fellow townsmen Han Nei, Ji Fu, and others; he was made Bulwark-General and Marquis of Hejian, Chengxin Illustrious Might General, and all were treated as honored guests and granted slaves, cattle, horses, and colored silks.

sentences.zh: 遂納颺女，是為文昭皇后，生世宗。

translations.literal: Thereupon he married Yang's daughter, who became Empress Wenzhao and bore Emperor Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then married Yang's daughter, who became Empress Wenzhao and bore the future Emperor Shizong.

sentences.zh: 颺卒。

translations.literal: Yang died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang died.

sentences.zh: 景明初，世宗追思舅氏，徵肇兄弟等。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, Emperor Shizong recalled his maternal kin and summoned Zhao and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jingming era Emperor Shizong, mindful of his mother's family, summoned Zhao and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 錄尚書事、北海王詳等奏：「颺宜贈左光祿大夫，賜爵勃海公，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Secretariat, the Prince of Beihai Xiang, and others memorialized: "Yang should be posthumously granted Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Bohai, and given the posthumous title Jing."
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Prince of Beihai Xiang, and others submitted a memorial: "Yang should be posthumously granted Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Bohai, and given the posthumous title Jing."

sentences.zh: 其妻蓋氏宜追封清河郡君。

translations.literal: His wife, the Lady Gai, should be posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Qinghe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Gai, should be posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Qinghe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved by edict.

sentences.zh: 又詔颺嫡孫猛襲勃海公爵，封肇平原郡公，肇弟顯澄城郡公。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered that Yang's eldest grandson's son Meng succeed to the ducal title of Bohai, enfeoffed Zhao as Duke of Pingyuan Commandery, and Zhao's younger brother Xian as Duke of Chengcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict named Yang's eldest grandson's son Meng successor to the ducal title of Bohai, enfeoffed Zhao as Duke of Pingyuan Commandery, and Zhao's younger brother Xian as Duke of Chengcheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 三人同日受封。

translations.literal: All three received enfeoffment on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: All three received their titles on the same day.

sentences.zh: 始世宗未與舅氏相接，將拜爵，乃賜衣幘引見肇、顯于華林都亭。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Shizong had had no contact with his maternal kin; when he was about to confer titles, he granted them caps and robes and had Zhao and Xian brought before him at the Duting pavilion in Hualin Park.
translations.idiomatic: Until then Emperor Shizong had never met his mother's kin; when he was about to confer their titles, he had caps and robes given them and received Zhao and Xian at the Duting pavilion in Hualin Park.

sentences.zh: 皆甚惶懼，舉動失儀。

translations.literal: Both were greatly fearful and lost propriety in their bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Both were deeply frightened and so ill at ease that their deportment fell apart.

sentences.zh: 數日之間，富貴赫弈。

translations.literal: Within a few days their wealth and rank blazed forth.
translations.idiomatic: Within days their wealth and rank had risen to dazzling heights.

sentences.zh: 是年，咸陽王禧誅，財物珍寶奴婢田宅多入高氏。

translations.literal: That year the Prince of Xianyang Xi was executed, and much of his property, treasures, slaves, fields, and houses passed into the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Prince of Xianyang Xi was put to death, and much of his property, treasures, slaves, fields, and houses passed into the Gao clan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，肇為尚書左僕射、領吏部、冀州大中正，尚世宗姑高平公主，遷尚書令。

translations.literal: Before long Zhao became Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, concurrently head of the Ministry of Personnel and chief assessor of Ji Province, married Emperor Shizong's paternal aunt the Princess of Gaoping, and was promoted to Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhao was made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, concurrently head of the Ministry of Personnel and chief assessor of Ji Province; he married Emperor Shizong's paternal aunt, the Princess of Gaoping, and was then promoted to Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 肇出自夷土，時望輕之。

translations.literal: Zhao came from barbarian soil, and contemporary esteem for him was slight.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhao came from a frontier background, men of the time held him in low regard.

sentences.zh: 及在位居要，留心百揆，孜孜無倦，世咸謂之為能。

translations.literal: When he held an important post, he attended to the hundred affairs of state with tireless diligence, and the age widely called him capable.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held high office, he applied himself tirelessly to the hundred affairs of state, and his contemporaries widely judged him capable.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，六輔專政，後以咸陽王禧無事構逆，由是遂委信肇。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign the six chief ministers monopolized government; later, because the Prince of Xianyang Xi had plotted rebellion without cause, the emperor thereupon entrusted his confidence to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign the six chief ministers monopolized government; after Prince of Xianyang Xi was found to have plotted rebellion without cause, the emperor placed his trust in Zhao instead.

sentences.zh: 肇既無親族，頗結朋黨，附之者旬月超昇，背之者陷以大罪。

translations.literal: Zhao had no kin of his own and therefore formed factions extensively; those who attached themselves to him were promoted within a month, while those who turned away were trapped in grave crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had no kin of his own and therefore built up a faction; adherents were promoted within a month, while those who opposed him were ruined on grave charges.

sentences.zh: 以北海王詳位居其上，構殺之。

translations.literal: Because the Prince of Beihai Xiang stood above him in rank, he framed him and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Because Prince of Beihai Xiang outranked him, he framed him and brought about his death.

sentences.zh: 又說世宗防衞諸王，殆同囚禁。

translations.literal: He also urged Emperor Shizong to guard the princes so closely that it was nearly the same as imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: He also persuaded Emperor Shizong to guard the princes so closely that they were kept in conditions little short of imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 時順皇后暴崩，世議言肇為之。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Shun died suddenly, and public opinion said Zhao was responsible.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Shun died suddenly, public opinion held that Zhao was behind it.

sentences.zh: 皇子昌薨，僉謂王顯失於醫療，承肇意旨。

translations.literal: When the imperial son Chang died, all said Wang Xian had failed in medical treatment at Zhao's instigation.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial son Chang died, all agreed that Wang Xian had bungled his medical care at Zhao's direction.

sentences.zh: 及京兆王愉出為冀州刺史，畏肇恣擅，遂至不軌。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jingzhao Yu went out as Governor of Ji Province, fearing Zhao's arbitrary power, he came to commit misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu was sent out as Governor of Ji Province, fear of Zhao's arbitrary power drove him to misconduct.

sentences.zh: 肇又譖殺彭城王勰。

translations.literal: Zhao also slandered and had the Prince of Pengcheng Xie killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao also slandered Prince of Pengcheng Xie and brought about his death.

sentences.zh: 由是朝野側目，咸畏惡之。

translations.literal: Because of this court and countryside turned sidelong glances at him, and all feared and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside alike turned against him, and all feared and hated him.

sentences.zh: 因此專權，與奪任己。

translations.literal: Thereby he monopolized power and granted or withheld office as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He thus monopolized power and granted or withheld office entirely at his own pleasure.

sentences.zh: 又嘗與清河王懌於雲龍門外廡下，忽忿諍，大至紛紜。

translations.literal: He also once suddenly quarreled in anger with the Prince of Qinghe Yi beneath the colonnade outside the Cloud Dragon Gate, until the dispute grew extremely heated.
translations.idiomatic: He once broke into a furious quarrel with Prince of Qinghe Yi beneath the colonnade outside the Cloud Dragon Gate, and the dispute grew extremely heated.

sentences.zh: 太尉、高陽王雍和止之。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal, the Prince of Gaoyang Yong, reconciled them and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Prince of Gaoyang Yong intervened and separated them.

sentences.zh: 高后既立，愈見寵信。

translations.literal: After Empress Gao was installed, he was ever more favored and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Gao was installed, he grew ever more favored and trusted.

sentences.zh: 肇既當衡軸，每事任己，本無學識，動違禮度，好改先朝舊制，出情妄作，減削封秩，抑黜勳人。

translations.literal: Zhao, now holding the pivot of power, made every affair depend on himself; he had no learning to begin with, constantly violated ritual norms, loved to alter the old institutions of the former court, acted capriciously from personal whim, reduced enfeoffments and ranks, and suppressed and demoted men of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhao held the pivot of power he made every affair depend on himself; he had no learning to begin with, constantly violated ritual norms, loved to alter the former court's institutions, acted capriciously from personal whim, reduced enfeoffments and ranks, and suppressed men of merit.

sentences.zh: 由是怨聲盈路矣。

translations.literal: Because of this the sound of resentment filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Resentment filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，遷司徒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanchang he was transferred to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yanchang era he was made Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 雖貴登台鼎，猶以去要怏怏形乎辭色。

translations.literal: Although he had ascended to the rank of the tripods, he still showed displeasure in word and countenance at having left the key post.
translations.idiomatic: Although he had risen to one of the three highest offices, he still showed his displeasure in word and countenance at having left the key post.

sentences.zh: 眾咸嗤笑之。

translations.literal: The multitude all laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 父兄封贈雖久，竟不改瘞。

translations.literal: Although his father and elder brothers had long received posthumous enfeoffment, he never changed their burial.
translations.idiomatic: Although his father and elder brothers had long received posthumous honors, he never had their remains reinterred.

sentences.zh: 三年，乃詔令遷葬。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict finally ordered their reinterment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict finally ordered their reinterment.

sentences.zh: 肇不自臨赴，唯遣其兄子猛改服詣代，遷葬於鄉。

translations.literal: Zhao did not go in person; he only sent his elder brother's son Meng, who changed into mourning garb and went to Dai, to transfer the burial to their native place.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao did not go in person but only sent his elder brother's son Meng, who put on mourning garb and went to Dai to have the remains reinterred in their native place.

sentences.zh: 時人以肇無識，哂而不責也。

translations.literal: Men of the time, considering Zhao ignorant, laughed but did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries, judging Zhao ignorant, laughed at him but did not blame him.

sentences.zh: 其年，大舉征蜀，以肇為大將軍，都督諸軍為之節度。

translations.literal: That year a great campaign was launched against Shu; Zhao was made Grand General and given overall command of the armies to direct them.
translations.idiomatic: That year a great campaign was launched against Shu; Zhao was made Grand General with overall command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 與都督甄琛等二十餘人俱面辭世宗於東堂，親奉規略。

translations.literal: Together with more than twenty men including the commander Zhen Chen, he took leave of Emperor Shizong face to face in the Eastern Hall and personally received strategic instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Together with more than twenty commanders including Zhen Chen, he took leave of Emperor Shizong in the Eastern Hall and received the emperor's strategic instructions in person.

sentences.zh: 是日，肇所乘駿馬停於神虎門外，無故驚倒，轉臥渠中，鞍具瓦解，眾咸怪異。

translations.literal: That day the fine horse Zhao was riding stopped outside the Divine Tiger Gate, startled and fell for no reason, rolled over into a ditch, and its saddle and trappings came apart; the crowd all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: That day the fine horse Zhao was riding halted outside the Divine Tiger Gate, startled and fell for no reason, rolled into a ditch, and its saddle and trappings fell apart; everyone regarded it as an omen.

sentences.zh: 肇出，惡焉。

translations.literal: When Zhao went out, he took it as ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao set out, he took it as a bad omen.

sentences.zh: 四年，世宗崩，赦罷征軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Emperor Shizong died; an amnesty was proclaimed and the campaign army disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Emperor Shizong died; an amnesty was proclaimed and the campaign army was disbanded.

sentences.zh: 肅宗與肇及征南將軍元遙等書，稱諱言，以告凶問。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong wrote to Zhao and the southern campaign general Yuan Yao and others, using the tabooed name to announce the grievous news.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong wrote to Zhao, the southern campaign general Yuan Yao, and others, using the tabooed imperial name to announce the emperor's death.

sentences.zh: 肇承變哀愕，非唯仰慕，亦私憂身禍，朝夕悲泣，至于羸悴。

translations.literal: When Zhao received the change he was grieved and stunned; it was not only mourning for the departed but also private fear of disaster to himself, and he wept morning and evening until he was wasted and haggard.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao received the news he was stunned with grief; it was not only mourning for the departed emperor but also private fear for his own life, and he wept morning and evening until he was wasted and haggard.

sentences.zh: 將至，宿瀍澗驛亭，家人夜迎省之，皆不相視。

translations.literal: As he was about to arrive, he lodged at the post station at Chanjian; his family came out at night to greet and see him, but none would look at one another.
translations.idiomatic: As he neared the capital he lodged at the post station at Chanjian; his family came out at night to greet him, but none could bear to meet another's eyes.

sentences.zh: 直至闕下，衰服號哭，昇太極殿，奉喪盡哀。

translations.literal: He went straight to the palace gates, wailed in mourning garb, ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and attended the coffin with full grief.
translations.idiomatic: He went straight to the palace gates, wailed in mourning garb, ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and attended the coffin with full grief.

sentences.zh: 太尉高陽王先居西柏堂，專決庶事，與領軍于忠密欲除之。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal, the Prince of Gaoyang, had first taken up residence in the Western Cypress Hall and decided ordinary affairs on his own; together with the commander of the guards Yu Zhong he secretly wished to eliminate Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Prince of Gaoyang had first taken up residence in the Western Cypress Hall and decided ordinary affairs on his own; together with the commander of the guards Yu Zhong he secretly plotted to eliminate Zhao.

sentences.zh: 潛備壯士直寢邢豹、伊瓫生等十餘人於舍人省下。

translations.literal: They secretly stationed more than ten stalwart men of the inner guard, including Xing Bao and Yi Tousheng, below the Attendants' Office.
translations.idiomatic: They secretly stationed more than ten stalwart men of the inner guard, including Xing Bao and Yi Tousheng, below the Attendants' Office.

sentences.zh: 肇哭梓宮訖，於百官前引入西廊，清河王懌、任城王澄及諸王等皆竊言目之。

translations.literal: When Zhao had finished mourning before the imperial coffin, he was led before the officials into the western corridor; the Prince of Qinghe Yi, the Prince of Rencheng Cheng, and the other princes all whispered and watched him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao had finished mourning before the imperial coffin, he was led before the officials into the western corridor; Prince of Qinghe Yi, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, and the other princes all whispered and watched him.

sentences.zh: 肇入省，壯士搤而拉殺之。

translations.literal: When Zhao entered the office, the stalwarts seized him by the throat and strangled him to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao entered the office, the stalwarts seized him by the throat and strangled him to death.

sentences.zh: 下詔暴其罪惡，又云刑書未及，便至自盡，自餘親黨，悉無追問，削除職爵，葬以士禮。

translations.literal: An edict exposed his crimes, and also said that before the penal code could be applied he had come to take his own life; the rest of his kin were not pursued at all, his offices and titles were struck off, and he was buried with the rites due a common gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: An edict exposed his crimes and declared that before the penal code could be applied he had taken his own life; the rest of his kin were not pursued, his offices and titles were struck off, and he was buried with the rites due a common gentleman.

sentences.zh: 及昏，乃於厠門出其尸歸家。

translations.literal: At dusk his corpse was brought out through the privy gate and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk his corpse was brought out through the privy gate and taken home.

sentences.zh: 初，肇西征，行至函谷，車軸中折。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhao marched west on campaign and reached Hangu Pass, an axle broke in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhao marched west on campaign and reached Hangu Pass, an axle broke in the middle.

sentences.zh: 從者皆以為不獲吉還也。

translations.literal: His followers all thought he would not obtain a fortunate return.
translations.idiomatic: His followers all thought he would not return safely.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，令特贈營州刺史。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, she ordered a special posthumous grant as Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, she ordered a special posthumous grant as Governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，出帝贈使持節、侍中、中外諸軍事、太師、大丞相、太尉公、錄尚書事、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, Emperor Chuodi posthumously granted him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Internal and External, Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, Duke and Grand Marshal, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi, Emperor Chuodi posthumously granted him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Internal and External, Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, Duke and Grand Marshal, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 肇子植。

translations.literal: Zhao's son Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's son was Zhi.

sentences.zh: 自中書侍郎為濟州刺史，率州軍討破元愉，別將有功。

translations.literal: From Palace Secretariat Attendant he became Governor of Ji Province, led the provincial army to defeat and crush Yuan Yu, and as a separate commander performed meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: From Palace Secretariat Attendant he became Governor of Ji Province, led the provincial army to defeat Yuan Yu, and as a separate commander performed meritorious service.

sentences.zh: 當蒙封賞，不受，云：「家荷重恩，為國致效是其常節，何足以應進陟之報。

translations.literal: He ought to have received enfeoffment and reward, but he would not accept, saying: "My family has received heavy grace; to render service to the state is its ordinary duty—how could that suffice as grounds for advancement and reward?"
translations.idiomatic: He was due enfeoffment and reward but refused, saying: "My family has received heavy grace; serving the state is our ordinary duty—how could that suffice as grounds for advancement and reward?"

sentences.zh: 」懇惻發於至誠。

translations.literal: His earnest sincerity sprang from utmost truth.
translations.idiomatic: His earnest sincerity sprang from the depths of his heart.

sentences.zh: 歷青、相、朔、恒四州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He served successively as Governor of Qing, Xiang, Shuo, and Heng provinces, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as governor of Qing, Xiang, Shuo, and Heng provinces, then died.

sentences.zh: 植頻莅五州，皆清能著稱，當時號為良刺史。

translations.literal: Zhi repeatedly held five provinces and in each was renowned for integrity and ability; his contemporaries called him a good governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi held office in five provinces in all and in each was renowned for integrity and ability; his contemporaries called him a good governor.

sentences.zh: 贈安北將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Pacification-North General and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Pacification-North General and Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 肇長兄琨，早卒。

translations.literal: Zhao's eldest brother Kun died early.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's eldest brother Kun died young.

sentences.zh: 襲颺封勃海郡公，贈都督五州諸軍事、鎮東大將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He succeeded to Yang's enfeoffment as Duke of Bohai Commandery and was posthumously granted Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Five Provinces, Pacification-East Grand General, and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to Yang's enfeoffment as Duke of Bohai Commandery and was posthumously granted Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Five Provinces, Pacification-East Grand General, and Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 詔其子猛嗣。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his son Meng to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named his son Meng as successor.

sentences.zh: 猛，字豹兒。

translations.literal: Meng, courtesy name Bao'er.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, whose courtesy name was Bao'er.

sentences.zh: 尚長樂公主，即世宗同母妹也。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Changle, who was Emperor Shizong's younger sister by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Changle, Emperor Shizong's younger sister by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 拜駙馬都尉，歷位中書令。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Imperial Son-in-Law and rose to Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Imperial Son-in-Law and rose to Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出為雍州刺史，有能名。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Yong Province and gained a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Governor of Yong Province and gained a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 入為殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He entered court as Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Minister of Works and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted Minister of Works and Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，復贈太師、大丞相、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Chuodi he was again posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Chuodi he was again posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 公主無子。

translations.literal: The princess had no son.
translations.idiomatic: The princess had no son.

sentences.zh: 猛先在外有男，不敢令主知，臨終方言之，年幾三十矣。

translations.literal: Meng had earlier had a son while away from home and did not dare let his wife know; only at his deathbed did he speak of it—the boy was nearly thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Meng had earlier fathered a son while away from home and did not dare tell his wife; only on his deathbed did he speak of it—the boy was nearly thirty.

sentences.zh: 乃召為喪主，尋卒，無後。

translations.literal: He was then summoned to serve as chief mourner, but soon died, leaving no heir.
translations.idiomatic: The boy was then summoned to serve as chief mourner, but soon died himself, leaving no heir.

sentences.zh: 琨弟偃，字仲游。

translations.literal: Kun's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Zhongyou.
translations.idiomatic: Kun's younger brother was Yan, whose courtesy name was Zhongyou.

sentences.zh: 太和十年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the tenth year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 正始中，贈安東將軍、都督、青州刺史，諡曰莊侯。

translations.literal: During Zhengshi he was posthumously granted Pacification-East General, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Qing Province, with the posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengshi era he was posthumously granted Pacification-East General, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Qing Province, with the posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 景明四年，世宗納其女為貴嬪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingming Emperor Shizong took his daughter as Honored Concubine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jingming Emperor Shizong took his daughter as Honored Concubine.

sentences.zh: 及于順皇后崩，永平元年立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Empress Shun of the Yu clan died, in the first year of Yongping she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Shun of the Yu clan died, in the first year of Yongping she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 二年，八座奏封后母王氏為武邑郡君。

translations.literal: In the second year the eight chief ministers memorialized to enfeoff the empress's mother, the Lady Wang, as Lady of Wuyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the eight chief ministers memorialized to enfeoff the empress's mother, Lady Wang, as Lady of Wuyi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 偃弟壽，早卒。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Shou died early.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Shou died young.

sentences.zh: 壽弟即肇也。

translations.literal: Shou's younger brother was none other than Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's younger brother was Zhao himself.

sentences.zh: 肇弟顯，侍中、高麗國大中正，早卒。

translations.literal: Zhao's younger brother Xian, Palace Attendant and chief assessor of the state of Goguryeo, died early.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's younger brother Xian, who had been Palace Attendant and chief assessor of the state of Goguryeo, died young.

sentences.zh: 于勁，字鍾葵，太尉拔之子。

translations.literal: Yu Jin, courtesy name Zhongkui, was the son of the Grand Marshal Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin, whose courtesy name was Zhongkui, was the son of Grand Marshal Ba.

sentences.zh: 頗有武略。

translations.literal: He had considerable military talent.
translations.idiomatic: He had considerable military talent.

sentences.zh: 以功臣子，又以功績，位沃野鎮將，賜爵富昌子，拜征虜將軍。

translations.literal: As the son of a meritorious minister and again for his own achievements, he held the post of garrison commander of Woye, was granted the title Marquis of Fuchang, and was appointed Campaign-General.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of a meritorious minister and again for his own achievements, he was made garrison commander of Woye, granted the title Marquis of Fuchang, and appointed Campaign-General.

sentences.zh: 世宗納其女為后，封太原郡公。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong took his daughter as empress and enfeoffed him as Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong took his daughter as empress and enfeoffed him as Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 妻劉氏，為章武郡君。

translations.literal: His wife, the Lady Liu, was made Lady of Zhangwu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Liu, was made Lady of Zhangwu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 後拜征北將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Campaign-North General and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Campaign-North General and Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空，諡曰恭莊公。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Minister of Works with the posthumous title Duke Gongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted Minister of Works with the posthumous title Duke Gongzhuang.

sentences.zh: 自栗磾至勁，累世貴盛，一皇后，四贈公，三領軍，二尚書令，三開國公。

translations.literal: From Yili to Jin, generation after generation was noble and flourishing: one empress, four posthumous dukes, three commanders of the guards, two directors of the Imperial Secretariat, and three founding marquises.
translations.idiomatic: From Yili to Jin, generation after generation the house had been noble and flourishing: one empress, four posthumous dukes, three commanders of the guards, two directors of the Imperial Secretariat, and three founding marquises.

sentences.zh: [2]勁雖以后父，但以順后早崩，竟不居公輔。

translations.literal: [2] Although Jin was the empress's father, because Empress Shun died early he never held one of the chief ministerial posts.
translations.idiomatic: [2] Although Jin was the empress's father, because Empress Shun died early he never held one of the chief ministerial posts.

sentences.zh: 子暉，字宣明，后母弟也。

translations.literal: His son Hui, courtesy name Xuanming, was the empress's younger brother by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hui, whose courtesy name was Xuanming and who was the empress's younger brother by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 少有氣幹。

translations.literal: In youth he had spirit and resolve.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed spirit and resolve.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，位汾州刺史。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and held the post of Governor of Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title and served as Governor of Fen Province.

sentences.zh: 暉善事人，為尒朱榮所親，以女妻其子長孺。

translations.literal: Hui was skilled at dealing with people, was favored by Erzhu Rong, and gave his daughter in marriage to Rong's son Changru.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was skilled in winning people over; Erzhu Rong favored him, and he gave his daughter to Rong's son Changru in marriage.

sentences.zh: 歷侍中、河南尹，後兼尚書僕射、東南道行臺。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Palace Attendant and Intendant of Henan, and later concurrently Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Commissioner of the Southeastern Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Palace Attendant and Intendant of Henan, and later also as Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and commissioner of the southeastern circuit.

sentences.zh: 與齊獻武王討平羊侃於兗州。

translations.literal: Together with Prince Xianwu of Qi he suppressed Yang Kan at Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Prince Xianwu of Qi he suppressed Yang Kan in Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，害之。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he had him killed.

sentences.zh: 勁弟天恩，位內行長、遼西太守。

translations.literal: Jin's younger brother Tian'en held the posts of Director of the Inner Household and Governor of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's younger brother Tian'en was Director of the Inner Household and Governor of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平東將軍、燕州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title General Who Pacifies the East and the post of Governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 天恩子仁生，位太中大夫。

translations.literal: Tian'en's son Rensheng held the post of Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Tian'en's son Rensheng was a Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 仁生子安定，平原郡太守、高平郡都將。

translations.literal: Rensheng's son was Anding, Governor of Pingyuan Commandery and chief commander of Gaoping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Rensheng's son Anding was Governor of Pingyuan Commandery and chief commander of Gaoping Commandery.

translations.literal: [3] He died.
translations.idiomatic: [3] He died.

sentences.zh: 胡國珍，字世玉，安定臨涇人也。

translations.literal: Hu Guozhen, courtesy name Shiyu, was a native of Linjing in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guozhen, whose courtesy name was Shiyu, was a native of Linjing in Anding.

sentences.zh: 祖略，姚興渤海公姚逵平北府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lue was a staff adviser in the Northern Pacification Office under Yao Kui, Duke of Bohai, a descendant of Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lue had been a staff adviser in the Northern Pacification Office under Yao Kui, Duke of Bohai, a descendant of Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 父淵，赫連屈丐給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Yuan served Helian Qubugai as Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan served Helian Qubugai as Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 世祖克統萬，淵以降款之功賜爵武始侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu conquered Tongwan, Yuan was granted the title Marquis of Wushi for his merit in surrendering in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu conquered Tongwan, Yuan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wushi for surrendering in good faith.

sentences.zh: 後拜河州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Governor of He Province.

sentences.zh: 國珍少好學，雅尚清儉。

translations.literal: Guozhen from youth loved learning and prized purity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Guozhen loved learning and prized simplicity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 太和十五年襲爵，例降為伯。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Taihe he inherited the title, which by regulation was reduced to that of count.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 15 he inherited the title, which by regulation was reduced one rank to count.

sentences.zh: 女以選入掖庭，生肅宗，即靈太后也。

translations.literal: His daughter was chosen and entered the Rear Palace, bore Suzong, and was none other than Empress Dowager Ling.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was selected for the palace harem, bore Emperor Suzong, and became Empress Dowager Ling.

sentences.zh: 肅宗踐祚，以國珍為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Suzong ascended the throne, he made Guozhen Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, he appointed Guozhen Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，加侍中，封安定郡公，給甲第，賜帛布綿縠奴婢車馬牛甚厚。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, he was additionally made Palace Attendant, enfeoffed as Duke of Anding Commandery, given a first-class mansion, and richly granted silk, cloth, cotton, damask, slaves, chariots, horses, and oxen.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, he was additionally made Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Anding Commandery, given a first-class mansion, and lavishly granted silk, cloth, cotton, damask, slaves, chariots, horses, and cattle.

sentences.zh: 追崇國珍妻皇甫氏為京兆郡君，置守冢十戶。

translations.literal: Guozhen's wife, the Lady Huangfu, was posthumously honored as Lady of Jingzhao Commandery, and ten households were appointed to guard the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen's wife, Lady Huangfu, was posthumously honored as Lady of Jingzhao Commandery, and ten households were appointed to guard her tomb.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、任城王澄奏，安定公屬尊望重，親賢羣矚，宜出入禁中，參諮大務。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, memorialized: "Duke of Anding belongs to honored kin and carries heavy prestige; kin and worthies all look to him. He ought to enter and leave the forbidden quarters and take part in consulting on great affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Secretariat Prince of Rencheng Cheng memorialized: "Duke of Anding is the empress's honored kin and carries great prestige; the court looks to him. He should have access to the inner palace and a voice in weighty affairs."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 乃令入決萬幾。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to enter and decide the ten thousand affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then authorized to enter the inner court and decide state affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋進位中書監、儀同三司，侍中如故，賞賜累萬。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and granted the Three Precedents of Honor, retaining his post as Palace Attendant; rewards piled to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat with the Three Precedents of Honor while retaining his post as Palace Attendant, and rewards ran into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 又賜絹歲八百匹，妻梁四百匹，男女姊妹兄弟各有差，皆極豐贍。

translations.literal: He was also granted eight hundred bolts of silk annually; his wife Lady Liang four hundred; sons and daughters, sisters, and brothers each differing amounts—all extremely generous.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted eight hundred bolts of silk each year; his wife Lady Liang received four hundred; sons, daughters, sisters, and brothers each received differing amounts—all lavish beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 國珍與太師、高陽王雍，太傅、清河王懌，太保、廣平王懷，入居門下，同釐庶政。

translations.literal: Guozhen together with the Grand Preceptor, Prince of Gaoyang Yong, the Grand Tutor, Prince of Qinghe Yi, and the Grand Guardian, Prince of Guangping Huai, entered residence at the Gate beneath and together regulated common government.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen joined Grand Preceptor Prince of Gaoyang Yong, Grand Tutor Prince of Qinghe Yi, and Grand Guardian Prince of Guangping Huai in residence at the Gate beneath the emperor to oversee ordinary government together.

sentences.zh: 詔依漢車千秋、晉安平王故事，給步挽一乘，自掖門至于宣光殿得以出入，并備几杖。

translations.literal: An edict followed the precedents of Han's Che Qianqiu and Jin's Prince of Ping'an, granting one hand-drawn carriage; from the Rear Gate to the Xuanguang Hall he might enter and leave, and was also provided with folding stool and staff.
translations.idiomatic: By edict, following the precedents of Han's Che Qianqiu and Jin's Prince of Ping'an, he was granted a hand-drawn carriage and might pass from the Rear Gate to Xuanguang Hall; he was also provided with a folding stool and staff.

sentences.zh: 後與侍中崔光俱授帝經，侍直禁中。

translations.literal: Later he and Palace Attendant Cui Guang together instructed the emperor in the classics, attending duty within the forbidden quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Palace Attendant Cui Guang together instructed the emperor in the classics, standing duty in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 國珍尋上表，陳刑政之宜。

translations.literal: Before long Guozhen submitted a memorial setting forth what was fitting in punishments and government.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Guozhen submitted a memorial on what was fitting in law and administration.

sentences.zh: 詔皆施行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all of it implemented.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered all of it carried out.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，[4]加國珍使持節、都督、雍州刺史、驃騎大將軍、開府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping, [4] Guozhen was additionally granted the Staff of Authority, made commissioner, Governor of Yong Province, Rapid Cavalry General-in-Chief, and Director of an Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Xiping, [4] Guozhen was additionally granted the ceremonial staff, made commissioner and Governor of Yong Province, appointed Rapid Cavalry General-in-Chief, and given an opening office.

sentences.zh: 靈太后以國珍年老，不欲令其在外，且欲示以方面之榮，竟不行。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling, because Guozhen was old, did not wish to have him outside the capital, yet wished to show him the glory of a frontier commission; in the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling, finding Guozhen too old to send away, still wished to confer the honor of a regional command on him; in the end he never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒公，侍中如故，就宅拜之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works, retaining his post as Palace Attendant; the appointment was conferred at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Works while retaining his post as Palace Attendant, and the appointment was conferred at his home.

sentences.zh: 靈太后、肅宗率百僚幸其第，宴會極歡。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling and Suzong led the hundred officials to visit his mansion; the feast was one of the greatest joy.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling and Emperor Suzong led the hundred officials to his mansion, where the feast reached the height of conviviality.

sentences.zh: 又追京兆郡君為秦太上君。

translations.literal: Lady of Jingzhao Commandery was again posthumously honored as Grand Supremacy Lady of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Jingzhao Commandery was again posthumously honored as Grand Supremacy Lady of Qin.

sentences.zh: [5]太上君景明三年薨於洛陽，於此十六年矣。

translations.literal: [5] The Grand Supremacy Lady died in Luoyang in the third year of Jingming; it had now been sixteen years.
translations.idiomatic: [5] The Grand Supremacy Lady had died in Luoyang in Jingming year 3; sixteen years had now passed.

sentences.zh: 太后以太上君墳瘞卑局，更增廣，為起塋域門闕碑表。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, because the Grand Supremacy Lady's tomb was low and cramped, further enlarged it, raising a burial domain, gate towers, stele, and marker.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Grand Supremacy Lady's tomb precinct was too small, the empress dowager enlarged it and erected a burial park with gate towers, steles, and markers.

sentences.zh: 侍中崔光等奏：「案漢高祖母始諡曰昭靈夫人，後為昭靈后，薄太后母曰靈文夫人，皆置園邑三百家，長丞奉守。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Cui Guang and others memorialized: "According to the precedents, Emperor Gao of Han's mother was at first given the posthumous title Lady Zhaoling, later Empress Zhaoling; Empress Dowager Bo's mother was titled Lady Lingwen—all had park-estates of three hundred households with wardens and attendants to maintain them.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Cui Guang and others memorialized: "By precedent, Emperor Gao of Han's mother was first titled Lady Zhaoling and later Empress Zhaoling; Empress Dowager Bo's mother was titled Lady Lingwen—all were given park-estates of three hundred households with wardens and attendants to maintain them.

sentences.zh: 今秦太上君未有尊諡，陵寢孤立，即秦君名，宜上終稱，兼設掃衞，以慰情典。

translations.literal: Now the Grand Supremacy Lady of Qin has no honored posthumous title; her tomb stands alone. Following the Qin lady's name, a final designation ought to be conferred, together with sweepers and guards, to satisfy ritual sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Supremacy Lady of Qin has no honored posthumous title and her tomb stands alone. Following the Qin lady's name, a final title ought to be conferred, with sweepers and guards appointed, to satisfy ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 請上尊諡曰孝穆，權置園邑三十戶，立長丞奉守。

translations.literal: We request that the honored posthumous title Xiaomu be conferred, and provisionally a park-estate of thirty households be established, with wardens and attendants appointed to maintain it.
translations.idiomatic: We request the posthumous title Xiaomu and provisionally a park-estate of thirty households, with wardens and attendants appointed to maintain it.

sentences.zh: 」太后從之。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager agreed.

sentences.zh: 封國珍繼室梁氏為趙平郡君，元叉妻拜為女侍中，封新平郡君，又徙封馮翊君。

translations.literal: Guozhen's successor wife Lady Liang was enfeoffed as Lady of Zhaoping Commandery; Yuan Cha's wife was appointed Female Palace Attendant, enfeoffed as Lady of Xinping Commandery, and later transferred to Lady of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen's second wife, Lady Liang, was enfeoffed as Lady of Zhaoping Commandery; Yuan Cha's wife was appointed Female Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Lady of Xinping Commandery, later transferred to Lady of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 國珍子祥妻長安縣公主，即清河王懌女也。

translations.literal: Guozhen's son Xiang's wife was the Princess of Chang'an County, who was the daughter of Prince of Qinghe Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen's son Xiang married the Princess of Chang'an County, daughter of Prince of Qinghe Yi.

sentences.zh: 國珍年雖篤老，而雅敬佛法，時事齋潔，自強禮拜。

translations.literal: Although Guozhen was deeply aged, he reverenced the Buddhist Law and at times observed purification and fasting, forcing himself to perform prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: Though greatly aged, Guozhen reverenced Buddhism, kept periods of purification and fasting, and forced himself to perform prostrations.

sentences.zh: 至於出入侍從，猶能跨馬據鞍。

translations.literal: Even in going out and in with attendants in attendance, he could still mount a horse and grip the saddle.
translations.idiomatic: When he went abroad with his attendants he could still mount a horse and hold the saddle.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年四月七日，步從所建佛像，發第至閶闔門四五里。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the fourth month of the first year of Shengui, on foot he followed the Buddha-image he had erected from his mansion to within four or five li of the Chongle Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the fourth month of Shengui year 1, he walked on foot following the Buddha image he had commissioned from his mansion to within four or five li of Chongle Gate.

sentences.zh: 八日，又立觀像，晚乃肯坐。

translations.literal: On the eighth he again stood viewing the image and only late would consent to sit.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth he again stood viewing the image and would not sit until evening.

sentences.zh: 勞熱增甚，因遂寢疾。

translations.literal: His fatigue and fever grew severe, and he thereupon took to his sickbed.
translations.idiomatic: Fatigue and fever worsened, and he took to his bed.

sentences.zh: 靈太后親侍藥膳。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling personally attended his medicines and food.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling personally attended his medicines and meals.

sentences.zh: 十二日薨，年八十。

translations.literal: On the twelfth he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the twelfth, aged eighty.

sentences.zh: 給東園溫明祕器、五時朝服各一具、衣一襲，贈布五千匹、錢一百萬、蠟千斤。

translations.literal: He was granted the warm bright secret coffin of the Eastern Garden, one set each of seasonal court robes, one suit of clothing, and posthumously granted five thousand bolts of cloth, a million cash, and a thousand jin of wax.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the warm bright coffin from the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes for each season, one suit of garments, and five thousand bolts of cloth, a million cash, and a thousand jin of wax.

sentences.zh: 大鴻臚持節監護喪事。

translations.literal: The Grand Herald, bearing the Staff of Authority, supervised the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Herald supervised the funeral bearing the ceremonial staff.

sentences.zh: 太后還宮，成服於九龍殿，遂居九龍寢室。

translations.literal: The empress dowager returned to the palace, donned mourning garments in the Hall of Nine Dragons, and thereupon dwelt in the Nine Dragons sleeping chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager returned to the palace, donned mourning in the Hall of Nine Dragons, and took up residence in the Nine Dragons bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 肅宗服小功服，舉哀於太極東堂。

translations.literal: Suzong wore the xiaogong degree of mourning and raised lamentation in the eastern hall of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong wore the third-degree mourning garments and raised lamentation in the eastern hall of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 又詔自始薨至七七，皆為設千僧齋，令七人出家；

translations.literal: An edict also ordered that from the beginning of death through the seven sevens, thousand-monk feasts were to be held each time, with seven persons ordained;
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered thousand-monk feasts for each observance from the day of death through the forty-nine days, with seven persons ordained each time;

sentences.zh: 百日設萬人齋，二七人出家。

translations.literal: on the hundredth day a ten-thousand-person feast, with twenty-seven persons ordained.
translations.idiomatic: on the hundredth day a feast for ten thousand, with twenty-seven persons ordained.

sentences.zh: 先是巫覡言將有凶，勸令為厭勝之法。

translations.literal: Earlier shamans and diviners had said there would be misfortune and urged him to perform exorcistic methods of overcoming it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier shamans and diviners had foretold disaster and urged exorcistic rites.

sentences.zh: 國珍拒而不從，云吉凶有定分，唯修德以禳之。

translations.literal: Guozhen refused and would not follow, saying fortune and misfortune have a fixed allotment, and one can only avert them by cultivating virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen refused, saying fortune and misfortune are allotted and can only be warded off by cultivating virtue.

sentences.zh: 臨死與太后訣云：「母子善治天下，以萬人之心，勿視大臣面也。

translations.literal: At death he took leave of the empress dowager, saying: "Mother and son, govern the realm well; with the heart of the myriad people—
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he bade farewell to the empress dowager, saying, "Mother and son, govern the realm well; with the hearts of the myriad people—

sentences.zh: 」殷勤至於再三。

translations.literal: do not look only to the ministers' faces." He urged this earnestly again and again.
translations.idiomatic: do not look only to the ministers' faces." He urged this again and again.

sentences.zh: 又及其子祥，云：「我唯有一子，死後勿如比來威抑之。

translations.literal: He also addressed his son Xiang, saying: "I have only this one son; after my death do not, as recently, suppress him by severity
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke to his son Xiang, saying, "I have only this one son; after my death do not restrain him with severity as you have lately

sentences.zh: 」靈太后以其好戲，時加威訓。

translations.literal: ." Empress Dowager Ling, because he was fond of play, at times applied stern admonition.
translations.idiomatic: ." Because Xiang was fond of play, Empress Dowager Ling had often disciplined him sternly.

sentences.zh: 國珍故以為言。

translations.literal: Guozhen therefore spoke thus on his account.
translations.idiomatic: That was what Guozhen had in mind when he said it.

sentences.zh: 始國珍欲就祖父西葬舊鄉，後緣前世諸胡多在洛葬，有終洛之心。

translations.literal: At first Guozhen wished to follow his grandfather and be buried in the west in his old home; later, because in previous generations many barbarians had been buried at Luoyang, he came to have the mind to end his days at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At first Guozhen had wished to join his grandfather in burial back west in his old home; later, seeing that many families of their kind had been buried at Luoyang for generations, he came to want his end there too.

sentences.zh: 崔光嘗對太后前問國珍：「公萬年後為在此安厝，為歸長安？

translations.literal: Cui Guang once before the empress dowager asked Guozhen: "When you reach ten thousand years, will you be laid to rest here, or return to Chang'an?
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang once asked Guozhen before the empress dowager, "When the time comes, will you be laid to rest here or return to Chang'an?

sentences.zh: 」國珍言當陪葬天子山陵。

translations.literal: Guozhen replied that he ought to be buried alongside the Son of Heaven in the imperial mountain tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen replied that he would be buried in the imperial mausoleum alongside the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 及病危，太后請以後事，竟言還安定，語遂昏忽。

translations.literal: When his illness grew critical, the empress dowager asked about his last affairs; in the end he spoke of returning to Anding, and his words then grew confused.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell critically ill, the empress dowager asked about his last wishes; in the end he spoke of returning to Anding, then his words grew confused.

sentences.zh: 太后問清河王懌與崔光等，議去留。

translations.literal: The empress dowager asked Prince of Qinghe Yi and Cui Guang and the others to discuss whether to leave the body or take it away.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager asked Prince of Qinghe Yi, Cui Guang, and the others to deliberate whether the burial should be at Luoyang or in the west.

sentences.zh: 懌等皆以病亂，請從先言。

translations.literal: Yi and the others all cited the disorder of illness and requested to follow his earlier words.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and the others cited the confusion of his illness and urged following his earlier statement.

sentences.zh: 太后猶記崔光昔與國珍言，遂營墓於洛陽。

translations.literal: The empress dowager still remembered what Cui Guang had once said with Guozhen, and therefore had a tomb prepared at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager still remembered Cui Guang's earlier exchange with Guozhen and had a tomb prepared at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 太后雖外從眾議，而深追臨終之語，云：「我公之遠慕二親，亦吾之思父母也。」

translations.literal: Although outwardly the empress dowager followed the multitude's deliberation, inwardly she deeply recalled his dying words, saying: "My lord's distant longing for his two parents is also my yearning for my parents."
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly the empress dowager followed the court's decision, yet she deeply mourned his dying wish, saying, "My lord's longing for his parents in the far west is also my longing for my own parents."

sentences.zh: 追崇假黃鉞、使持節、侍中、相國、都督中外諸軍事、太師、領太尉公、司州牧，號太上秦公，加九錫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored with the provisional Yellow Axe, Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Chancellor of State, Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, Grand Preceptor, concurrently Duke of Grand Commandant, Governor of Si Province, titled Grand Supremacy Duke of Qin, with the Nine Bestowals added.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with the ceremonial axe and staff, named Palace Attendant, Chancellor of State, commander-in-chief of all armies, Grand Preceptor, concurrently Duke of Grand Commandant and Governor of Si Province, titled Grand Supremacy Duke of Qin, and granted the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 葬以殊禮，給九旒鑾輅，虎賁、班劍百人，前後部羽葆鼓吹，轀輬車；

translations.literal: He was buried with extraordinary rites, granted the nine tassels and imperial chariot, a hundred tiger guards and ceremonial swords, front and rear feather-canopy processional music, and a pall carriage;
translations.idiomatic: He was buried with extraordinary rites: the nine tassels and imperial chariot, a hundred tiger guards and ceremonial swords, front and rear feather-canopy musicians, and a pall carriage;

sentences.zh: 諡文宣公；

translations.literal: posthumous title Duke Wenxuan;
translations.idiomatic: posthumous title Duke Wenxuan;

sentences.zh: 賜物三千段、粟一千五百石。

translations.literal: granted three thousand lengths of goods and fifteen hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: three thousand lengths of goods and fifteen hundred piculs of grain were granted.

sentences.zh: 又詔贈國珍祖父兄、父兄，下逮從子，皆有封職。

translations.literal: An edict also posthumously granted Guozhen's grandfather's elder brother, father's elder brother, and down to younger cousins—all received enfeoffments and offices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also posthumously enfeoffed Guozhen's grandfather's and father's elder brothers and conferred ranks down to his cousins.

sentences.zh: 持節就安定監護喪事。

translations.literal: Bearing the Staff of Authority, officials went to Anding to supervise the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Officials bearing the ceremonial staff went to Anding to supervise the funeral.

sentences.zh: [6]靈太后迎太上君神柩還第，與國珍俱葬，贈襚一與國珍同。

translations.literal: [6] Empress Dowager Ling welcomed the Grand Supremacy Lady's spirit coffin back to the mansion and buried her together with Guozhen; funeral gifts were the same as for Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: [6] Empress Dowager Ling brought the Grand Supremacy Lady's spirit coffin back to the mansion and buried her with Guozhen; her funeral gifts matched his.

sentences.zh: 及國珍神主入廟，詔太常權給以軒懸之樂、六佾之舞。

translations.literal: When Guozhen's spirit tablet entered the ancestral temple, an edict ordered the Minister of Ceremonies provisionally to grant the suspended bells and drums music and the six rows of dancers.
translations.idiomatic: When Guozhen's spirit tablet entered the ancestral temple, the Minister of Ceremonies was ordered provisionally to grant the full royal music and six rows of dancers.

sentences.zh: 初國珍無男，養兄真子僧洗為後，後納趙平君，生子祥。

translations.literal: At first Guozhen had no son; he adopted his elder brother Zhen's son Sengxi as heir, and later took Lady of Zhaoping as consort and bore the son Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: At first Guozhen had no sons; he adopted his elder brother Zhen's son Sengxi as heir, and later took Lady of Zhaoping and bore Xiang.

sentences.zh: 僧洗，字湛輝。

translations.literal: Sengxi, courtesy name Zhanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Sengxi, whose courtesy name was Zhanhui.

sentences.zh: 封爰德縣公，位中書監、侍中，改封濮陽郡公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Duke of Aide County, held the posts of Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and Palace Attendant, and was later transferred to Duke of Puyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Duke of Aide County, served as Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and Palace Attendant, and was later made Duke of Puyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 僧洗自永安後廢棄，不預朝政。

translations.literal: From after Yongan onward Sengxi was cast aside and did not participate in court government.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongan, Sengxi was cast aside and took no part in government.

sentences.zh: 天平四年薨，詔給東園祕器，贈太師、太尉公、錄尚書事、雍州刺史，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianping he died; an edict granted the secret coffin of the Eastern Garden, posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Commandant, Recorder of Affairs of the Imperial Secretariat, and Governor of Yong Province, posthumous title Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tianping year 4; he was granted the Eastern Garden coffin and posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Commandant, Recorder of Affairs of the Imperial Secretariat, and Governor of Yong Province, with the posthumous title Xiao.

sentences.zh: 真長子寧，[7]字惠歸。

translations.literal: Zhen's eldest son was Ning, [7] courtesy name Huigui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's eldest son was Ning, [7] whose courtesy name was Huigui.

sentences.zh: 襲國珍先爵，改為臨涇伯，後進為公。

translations.literal: He inherited Guozhen's former title, which was changed to Marquis of Linjing, and was later promoted to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited Guozhen's former rank, which was changed to Count of Linjing and later raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 歷岐涇二州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively held the governorships of Qi and Jing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as governor of Qi and Jing provinces.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰孝穆。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Xiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Xiaomu.

sentences.zh: 女為清河王亶妃，生孝靜皇帝。

translations.literal: His daughter was consort to Prince of Qinghe Tan and bore Emperor Xiaojing.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was consort to Prince of Qinghe Tan and bore Emperor Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: 武定初，贈太師、太尉公、錄尚書事，諡曰孝昭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Commandant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Imperial Secretariat, posthumous title Xiaozhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Wuding he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Commandant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Imperial Secretariat, with the posthumous title Xiaozhao.

sentences.zh: 子虔，字僧敬。

translations.literal: His son Qian, courtesy name Sengjing.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Qian, whose courtesy name was Sengjing.

sentences.zh: 元叉之廢靈太后，虔時為千牛備身，與備身張車渠等謀殺叉。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling, Qian was at the time a gentleman guard of the Thousand-Ox Corps and with gentleman guard Zhang Chequ and others plotted to kill Cha.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling, Qian was a gentleman guard of the Thousand-Ox Corps and plotted with fellow guard Zhang Chequ and others to kill Cha.

sentences.zh: 事發，叉殺車渠等，虔坐遠徙。

translations.literal: When the affair broke out, Cha killed Chequ and the others; Qian was punished by exile to a distant place.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, Cha executed Chequ and the others; Qian was exiled to a distant post.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，徵為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling restored her rule, he was summoned as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling resumed power, he was recalled as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 太后好以家人禮與親族宴戲，虔常致諫，由是後宴謔多不預焉。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was fond of using family ritual to feast and jest with kin; Qian often remonstrated, and for this reason afterward he often did not take part in such banquets and play.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager liked to entertain her kin in informal family style; Qian often remonstrated, and thereafter was often left out of such feasts and games.

sentences.zh: 出為涇州刺史，封安陽縣侯。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Jing Province and was enfeoffed Marquis of Anyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Governor of Jing Province and enfeoffed as Marquis of Anyang County.

sentences.zh: 興和三年，以帝元舅超遷司空公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xinghe, because he was the emperor's maternal uncle by the original line, he was super-promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Xinghe year 3, as the emperor's chief maternal uncle, he was promoted outright to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太傅、太尉公、尚書僕射、徐州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, Duke of Grand Commandant, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Governor of Xu Province, posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor, Duke of Grand Commandant, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Governor of Xu Province, with the posthumous title Xuan.

sentences.zh: 葬日，百官會葬，乘輿送於郭外。

translations.literal: On the day of burial all officials attended the funeral, and the imperial carriage escorted the coffin beyond the outer wall of the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial all officials attended the funeral, and the imperial carriage escorted the coffin beyond the city walls.

sentences.zh: 子長粲。

translations.literal: His son Changcan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Changcan.

sentences.zh: 李延寔，字禧，隴西人，尚書僕射沖之長子。

translations.literal: Li Yanshi, courtesy name Xi, was a native of Longxi and the eldest son of Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanshi, whose courtesy name was Xi, was a native of Longxi and the eldest son of Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 性溫良，少為太子舍人。

translations.literal: His nature was gentle and good; in youth he served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle by nature, in youth he served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，襲父爵清泉縣侯。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign he inherited his father's title as Marquis of Qingquan County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign he inherited his father's title as Marquis of Qingquan County.

sentences.zh: [8]累遷左將軍、光州刺史。

translations.literal: [8] He was promoted in succession to Left General and Governor of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: [8] He rose in succession to Left General and Governor of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 莊帝即位，以元舅之尊，超授侍中、太保，封濮陽郡王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangdi ascended the throne, in honor of his status as the emperor's maternal uncle he was exceptionally appointed Palace Attendant and Grand Guardian and enfeoffed as Prince of Puyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangdi ascended the throne, in honor of his status as the emperor's maternal uncle he was exceptionally appointed Palace Attendant and Grand Guardian and enfeoffed as Prince of Puyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 延寔以太保犯祖諱，又以王爵非庶姓所宜，抗表固辭。

translations.literal: Yanshi, because Grand Guardian violated the imperial ancestral taboo and because a princely title was not fitting for a common surname, submitted a memorial firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi submitted a firm memorial of refusal, arguing that Grand Guardian violated the imperial ancestral taboo and that a princely title was not fitting for a common surname.

sentences.zh: 徙封濮陽郡公，改授太傅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Duke of Puyang Commandery and instead appointed Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Duke of Puyang Commandery and appointed Grand Tutor instead.

sentences.zh: 尋轉司徒公，出為使持節、侍中、太傅、錄尚書事、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Education, then sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Tutor, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Minister of Education, then sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Tutor, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆入洛，乘輿幽縶，以延寔外戚，見害於州館。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang and the imperial carriage was held in confinement, Yanshi, as maternal kin, was killed in the provincial residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang and the emperor was held captive, Yanshi, as maternal kin, was killed in the provincial residence.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，歸葬洛陽。

translations.literal: Early under Emperor Chuodi his remains were returned for burial at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early under Emperor Chuodi his remains were returned for burial at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、侍中、太師、太尉公、錄尚書事、都督、雍州刺史，諡曰孝懿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Duke and Grand Marshal, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Yong Province, with the posthumous title Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Duke and Grand Marshal, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Yong Province, with the posthumous title Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 長子彧，字子文，尚莊帝姊豐亭公主。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yu, courtesy name Ziwen, married the Princess of Fengting, elder sister of Emperor Zhuangdi.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Yu, whose courtesy name was Ziwen; he married the Princess of Fengting, Emperor Zhuangdi's elder sister.

sentences.zh: 封東平郡公，位侍中、左光祿大夫、中書監、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping Commandery and held the posts of Palace Attendant, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, Swift Cavalry Grand General, and Grand Guardian with the Bountiful Rites Equal to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping Commandery and held the posts of Palace Attendant, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, Swift Cavalry Grand General, Grand Guardian with the Bountiful Rites Equal to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 彧任俠交遊，輕薄無行。

translations.literal: Yu was chivalrous in making friends and frivolous in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yu cultivated chivalrous friendships but was frivolous and unprincipled in conduct.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之死也，武毅之士皆彧所進。

translations.literal: At the death of Erzhu Rong, the bold and resolute warriors had all been introduced by Yu.
translations.idiomatic: At Erzhu Rong's death, the bold warriors who struck the blow had all been introduced by Yu.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，以罪棄市。

translations.literal: Early in Xiaojing's reign he was executed in the marketplace for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was executed in the marketplace for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：三五哲王，深防遠慮。

translations.literal: The historian says: The sage kings of the Three Dynasties and the Five Emperors took deep precautions and looked far ahead.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The sage kings of the Three Dynasties and the Five Emperors took deep precautions and looked far ahead.

sentences.zh: 舅甥之國，罕執鈞衡；

translations.literal: In states ruled by uncle and nephew, few held the balance of power;
translations.idiomatic: In states ruled by uncle and nephew, few held the balance of power;

sentences.zh: 母后之家，無聞傾敗。

translations.literal: among the families of empresses dowager and queens, one never heard of ruin and overthrow.
translations.idiomatic: among the families of empresses dowager and queens, one never heard of ruin and overthrow.

sentences.zh: 爰及後世，顛覆繼軌。

translations.literal: But when it came to later ages, overthrow followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: But in later ages overthrow followed in succession.

sentences.zh: 蓋由進不以禮，故其斃亦速。

translations.literal: This was because advancement did not follow ritual propriety, and so their destruction was also swift.
translations.idiomatic: This was because advancement did not follow ritual propriety, and so their destruction came swiftly as well.

sentences.zh: 其間或不泯舊基，[9]弗虧先構者，蓋處之以道，遠權之所致也。

translations.literal: Among them, those who did not extinguish the old foundation[9] or impair what their forebears had built did so because they were treated according to the Way and because distant authority was exercised.
translations.idiomatic: Those among them who did not extinguish the old foundation[9] or impair what their forebears had built did so because they were treated according to the Way and because distant authority was exercised over them.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual collation notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷八十三下 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」字，卷末有宋人校語

translations.literal: Book of Wei juan 83b: various editions' tables of contents mark this juan with the note "deficient"; at the end of the juan there is a Song-dynasty collation note
translations.idiomatic: Book of Wei, juan 83b: various editions' tables of contents mark this juan as deficient; at the end of the juan there is a Song-dynasty collation note

sentences.zh: 〈殿本入考證〉

translations.literal: 〈Entered into textual verification in the Palace Edition〉
translations.idiomatic: (Entered into textual verification in the Palace Edition)

sentences.zh: 云：「魏收書外戚傳亡，史臣論全用隋書外戚傳

translations.literal: stating: "Wei Shou's original Treatise on Maternal Kin is lost; the historian's discussion is entirely taken from the Sui shu Treatise on Maternal Kin
translations.idiomatic: stating: "Wei Shou's original Treatise on Maternal Kin is lost; the historian's discussion is entirely taken from the Sui shu Treatise on Maternal Kin

sentences.zh: 〈卷七九〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 79〉
translations.idiomatic: (juan 79)

sentences.zh: 」按此卷亦以北史卷八０外戚傳補。

translations.literal: " According to this, the present juan was also supplemented from the Northern History juan 80, Treatise on Maternal Kin.
translations.idiomatic: " This juan was also supplemented from the Northern History, juan 80, Treatise on Maternal Kin.

sentences.zh: 其于勁傳採北史卷三一于栗磾附于勁傳，李延寔傳採卷一００自序。

translations.literal: Its biography of Yu Jin draws on the Northern History juan 31, biography of Yu Libi with the appended biography of Yu Jin; the biography of Li Yanshi draws on juan 100, Author's Preface.
translations.idiomatic: Its biography of Yu Jin draws on the Northern History, juan 31, biography of Yu Libi with the appended biography of Yu Jin; the biography of Li Yanshi draws on juan 100, Author's Preface.

sentences.zh: 諸傳均有溢出語，當是以高氏小史等他書附益之。

translations.literal: All the biographies contain superfluous passages, presumably added from the Gao clan's Minor History and other books.
translations.idiomatic: All the biographies contain superfluous passages, presumably added from the Gao clan's Minor History and other books.

sentences.zh: 自栗磾至勁

translations.literal: From Yili to Jin
translations.idiomatic: From Yili to Jin

translations.literal: 〈to〉
translations.idiomatic: (to)

sentences.zh: 三開國公 按此數語魏書本在卷三一于栗磾附于忠傳後，北史卷二三于栗磾傳移在于勁傳中，則在後的于忠所歷官爵，不當計算在內，所舉贈公、領軍、尚書令、開國公便都少了一人，實誤。

translations.literal: three founding marquises: According to this, these words originally stood in the Book of Wei juan 31 after the appended biography of Yu Zhong in the biography of Yu Libi; the Northern History juan 23 biography of Yu Libi moved them into the biography of Yu Jin—then the offices and titles held by the later Yu Zhong should not be counted, and the tallies of posthumous dukes, commanders of the guards, directors of the Imperial Secretariat, and founding marquises are each one short—a real error.
translations.idiomatic: three founding marquises: These words originally stood in the Book of Wei, juan 31, after the appended biography of Yu Zhong in the biography of Yu Libi; the Northern History, juan 23, moved them into the biography of Yu Jin—then the offices held by the later Yu Zhong should not be counted, and the tallies of posthumous dukes, commanders of the guards, directors of the Imperial Secretariat, and founding marquises are each one short—a real error.

sentences.zh: 此傳以北史補，不記卷三一已有此語，以致複出。

translations.literal: This biography was supplemented from the Northern History without noting that juan 31 already contained these words, causing duplication.
translations.idiomatic: This biography was supplemented from the Northern History without noting that juan 31 already contained these words, causing duplication.

sentences.zh: 參卷三一校記[九]。

translations.literal: See the collation note [9] to juan 31.
translations.idiomatic: See the collation note [9] to juan 31.

sentences.zh: 高平郡都將 按郡無都將，「郡」當是「鎮」之訛。

translations.literal: chief commander of Gaoping Commandery: According to this, a commandery has no "chief commander"; "commandery" should be a corruption of "garrison."
translations.idiomatic: Chief commander of Gaoping Commandery: a commandery has no such post as "chief commander"; "commandery" should be a corruption of "garrison."

sentences.zh: 熙平初 諸本及北史卷八０胡國珍傳「熙平」作「延和」，通志卷一六五胡國珍傳作「熙平中」。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping: various editions and the Northern History juan 80 biography of Hu Guozhen read "Xiping" as "Yanhe"; the Tongzhi juan 165 biography of Hu Guozhen reads "mid-Xiping."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiping: various editions and the Northern History, juan 80, biography of Hu Guozhen read "Xiping" as "Yanhe"; the Tongzhi, juan 165, biography of Hu Guozhen reads "mid-Xiping."

sentences.zh: 按事見卷九肅宗紀熙平元年八月乙巳，延和乃拓跋燾年號，遠在其前。

translations.literal: According to this, the event appears in juan 9, Annals of Emperor Suzong, eighth month, day yisi of the first year of Xiping; Yanhe is the reign title of Tuoba Tao, far earlier.
translations.idiomatic: The event appears in juan 9, Annals of Emperor Suzong, eighth month, day yisi of the first year of Xiping; Yanhe is the reign title of Tuoba Tao, far earlier.

sentences.zh: 今據通志改作「熙平」。

translations.literal: Now, following the Tongzhi, it is emended to "Xiping."
translations.idiomatic: Following the Tongzhi, the text is emended to "Xiping."

sentences.zh: 事在元年，「初」字不誤。

translations.literal: The event falls in the first year; the word "beginning" is not in error.
translations.idiomatic: The event falls in the first year; the word "beginning" is not in error.

sentences.zh: 又追京兆郡君為秦太上君 按「追」下當脫「贈」或「尊」「崇」字。

translations.literal: Again, Lady of Jingzhao Commandery was posthumously honored as Grand Dowager of Qin: According to this, after "posthumously" the word "granted" or "honored" or "exalted" is missing.
translations.idiomatic: Again, Lady of Jingzhao Commandery was posthumously honored as Grand Dowager of Qin: After "posthumously" the word "granted," "honored," or "exalted" is missing.

sentences.zh: 持節就安定監護喪事 按胡國珍死和葬都在洛陽，何故「就安定監護喪事」？

translations.literal: Bearer of the Staff of Authority went to Anding to supervise the funeral: According to this, Hu Guozhen died and was buried at Luoyang—why "went to Anding to supervise the funeral"?
translations.idiomatic: Bearer of the Staff of Authority went to Anding to supervise the funeral: Hu Guozhen died and was buried at Luoyang—why does the text say he went to Anding to supervise the funeral?

sentences.zh: 下文云：「迎太上君神柩還第」，疑「安定」下脫「公第」二字。

translations.literal: The text below says, "The spirit coffin of the Grand Dowager was welcomed back to the residence"—it is suspected that after "Anding" the two characters "duke's residence" are missing.
translations.idiomatic: The text below says, "The spirit coffin of the Grand Dowager was welcomed back to the residence"—it is suspected that after "Anding" the two characters "duke's residence" are missing.

sentences.zh: 真長子寧 諸本「真」字連上段「諡曰孝」，「長子寧」提行。

translations.literal: Zhen's eldest son Ning: various editions join the character "Zhen" to the preceding passage "posthumous title Xiao," and begin a new line at "eldest son Ning."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's eldest son Ning: various editions join the character "Zhen" to the preceding passage "posthumous title Xiao," and begin a new line at "eldest son Ning."

sentences.zh: 成為胡僧洗諡「孝真」，「寧」是僧洗的長子。

translations.literal: This makes Hu Sengxi's posthumous title "Xiaozhen," and "Ning" Sengxi's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: This makes Hu Sengxi's posthumous title "Xiaozhen," and makes "Ning" Sengxi's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 按真乃國珍兄，見上文，寧乃僧洗兄。

translations.literal: According to this, Zhen was Guozhen's elder brother, as seen above, and Ning was Sengxi's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was Guozhen's elder brother, as seen above, and Ning was Sengxi's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 北史原文本不提行，後人寫刻魏書則凡附見諸子孫無不提行，這裏由於誤讀，提行亦謬，致以兄為子，今改正。

translations.literal: The Northern History original did not begin a new line; later copyists and printers of the Book of Wei always began a new line for every appended son or grandson—here through misreading the line break was also wrong, making an elder brother into a son; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern History original did not begin a new line; later copyists and printers of the Book of Wei always began a new line for every appended son or grandson—here misreading produced a wrong line break that made an elder brother into a son; the text is now corrected.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵清泉縣侯 按卷五三李沖傳，沖封「清淵縣侯」。

translations.literal: Inherited his father's title as Marquis of Qingquan County: According to juan 53, biography of Li Chong, Chong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qingyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: Inherited his father's title as Marquis of Qingquan County: According to juan 53, biography of Li Chong, Chong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qingyuan County.

sentences.zh: 「清淵」為漢以來舊縣，卷一０六上地形志上，屬司州陽平郡。

translations.literal: "Qingyuan" is an old county since Han times; juan 106a, Treatise on Geography, Part 1, places it in Yangping Commandery, Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: "Qingyuan" is an old county since Han times; juan 106a, Treatise on Geography, Part 1, places it in Yangping Commandery, Si Province.

sentences.zh: 此傳以北史補，避唐諱改「泉」。

translations.literal: This biography was supplemented from the Northern History; to avoid Tang taboo "yuan" was changed to "quan."
translations.idiomatic: This biography was supplemented from the Northern History; to avoid Tang taboo "yuan" was changed to "quan."

sentences.zh: 其間或不泯舊基 諸本「泯」上有「斃」字。

translations.literal: Among them, those who did not extinguish the old foundation: various editions have the character "destroyed" above "extinguish."
translations.idiomatic: Among them, those who did not extinguish the old foundation: various editions have the character "destroyed" above "extinguish."

sentences.zh: 此傳本出北史，北史傳論又本隋書卷七九外戚傳論，今檢隋書、北史都作「今或不隕舊基」，這裏「今或」作「其間」，「隕」作「泯」，均兩通，「斃」字則涉上「其斃亦速」而衍，今刪。

translations.literal: This treatise discussion originally comes from the Northern History, and the Northern History discussion in turn comes from the Sui shu juan 79 Treatise on Maternal Kin discussion; checking the Sui shu and Northern History, both read "now perhaps they do not fall from the old foundation"—here "now perhaps" is written as "among them" and "fall" as "extinguish," both acceptable; the character "destroyed" is a derivative from the preceding "their destruction was also swift" and is now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: This historian's discussion originally comes from the Northern History, which in turn draws on the Sui shu, juan 79, Treatise on Maternal Kin; checking the Sui shu and Northern History, both read "now perhaps they do not fall from the old foundation"—here "now perhaps" appears as "among them" and "fall" as "extinguish," both acceptable; the character "destroyed" is a derivative from the preceding "their destruction came swiftly" and is now deleted.
